LEARNING PATH LESSON · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Boxing — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches boxing the way good gyms do: stance and guard first, straight punches at PADS only, and the rule spoken out loud in every round — pads and bags, never people.

What is this?

Boxing is the punch sport with big gloves: guard up protecting the face, feet springy, straight jabs and crosses at pads, bags and nothing else. Real boxers are among the fittest athletes alive.

What does it mean?

For little ones, boxing is pad-work fitness: a strong stance, fast straight arms, bouncing feet — and the discipline of WHERE punching is allowed. The rule is not a warning on the side of the lesson; the rule is the lesson.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three boxing ideas: the guard — fists up by the cheeks, elbows in, protecting the face; the jab is STRAIGHT — out and back down the same road, fast; and the rule — pads, bags and cushions are the only targets, ever, in every round.

Why this matters

Pad rounds are pure joy — thirty seconds of jab-jab-cross with a roaring finish — and they build the strongest shoulders and straightest punches on this wall, inside the safest rule in sport.

What it teaches

Straight punching mechanics (out-and-back on one road), guard posture, springy footwork, thirty-second effort bursts, and rule-keeping under excitement — the deepest skill in the gym.

Words to learn

boxingguardjabcrosspadsroundstraight

Say this to your child

“"Boxing is the pad-punching sport! Fists up by your cheeks — that is the guard. Jab — straight out, straight back, one road. Jab, jab, CROSS! But here is the rule, and it never changes: we punch PADS and BAGS, never people, never pets, never walls. Boxers are the fittest, politest punchers in the world — the rule is why."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is boxing — the pad-punching fitness sport."
  2. The guard: fists up by the cheeks, elbows tucked, chin soft. Say the rule BEFORE the first punch: "pads and bags, never people."
  3. The jab: straight out from the cheek, straight back to the cheek — one road, out and home. Ten quiet jabs in the air.
  4. The cross: the other hand’s straight punch with a small hip turn — jab-jab-CROSS is the drumbeat.
  5. Play the pad rounds below and end every round with the rule, out loud: "pads and bags, never people."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "boxing" leads at the top in big letters with the gym’s scene below — the gloves and the training pads exactly as a pad-round looks.

Ask your child

"Where do the fists live in the guard? What road does the jab travel? What are the ONLY targets in boxing?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Guard up — fists by my cheeks!" "Jab, jab, CROSS!" or the rule, unprompted: "Pads and bags, never people!"

Out in the real world

Boxing gyms everywhere welcome kids’ pad-work classes — and every one of them teaches the same rule first. On screen, watch one pad round: the trainer’s pads are the only things the gloves ever touch. That is boxing’s own discipline, visible.

Try it together

Pad Rounds: grown-up holds cushions as pads. Round one: thirty seconds of jab-jab-cross, feet bouncing, big finish cheer. Round two: jab on the MOVE — follow the pads around the room. Round three: child’s choice, but the round must END with the rule said out loud. Three rounds, water break, guard-up parade lap. Fitness, straightness, and a rule kept with pride.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is the guard? What road does the jab take? What are the only targets?" Fists by the cheeks, out-and-back straight, pads and bags — three answers and the round is on.

Parent tips

Hold the pads LOW for little arms — shoulder height is grown-up height. And if any punch ever drifts toward a person, the round pauses instantly and calmly: the rule is the lesson, and pausing proves it — warmly, every time.

This lesson pairs with the Boxing flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sports & Movement (Class 37).
